explanation: For I, 1+tx>0 throughout the stated domain, and the partial derivative x/((1+tx)(1+x²)) is continuous locally in t. For II, t>1 keeps x-t nonzero, so the integrand and its partial derivative 1/(x-t)² are continuous. III is singular at x=t, and its partial derivative is not integrable there. Thus only I and II permit differentiation under the integral sign.
